# Observability contract

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-observability.js from src/runtime/observability-manifest.js. -->

Schema version: **1**.

This is the adapter-owned machine-readable contract exposed as
`svelte-adapter-uws/observability`. It defines the fields a conforming
structured event or log may use and the complete adapter metric inventory.
Sibling packages can consume and validate this schema; they retain ownership of
their own signal inventories. See the [package README](../README.md#cluster-wide-metrics)
for runtime setup and the [reference queries](../examples/observability/queries.md).

A schema-version change is required before removing a field, changing a unit,
widening a label domain, changing a data class, or changing a no-data law.
Additive signals within the same schema version still require generated-doc and
contract-test updates.

## Event and log envelope

Allowed levels: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`.

| Field | Required | Type | Data class | Domain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | yes | `integer` | `operational` | - |
| `occurredAt` | yes | `rfc3339-utc` | `operational` | - |
| `level` | yes | `enum` | `operational` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal` |
| `event` | yes | `dot-name` | `operational` | - |
| `component` | yes | `dot-name` | `operational` | - |
| `dataClass` | yes | `enum` | `operational` | `operational`, `pseudonymous`, `application`, `secret` |
| `requestId` | no | `printable-ascii-128` | `pseudonymous` | - |
| `traceparent` | no | `w3c-traceparent` | `pseudonymous` | - |
| `tracestate` | no | `w3c-tracestate` | `pseudonymous` | - |
| `attributes` | no | `object` | `application` | - |

The top-level `dataClass` is the most restrictive class carried anywhere in
the event. `event`, `component`, metric names, and metric labels are bounded
framework vocabulary: never copy a topic, user id, address, cookie, token,
payload, or arbitrary exception text into those fields. Application attributes
are omitted unless the deployer has classified and retained them deliberately.

## Correlation and trace context

| Field | Header | Adapter propagation | Data class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requestId` | `x-request-id` | supported | `pseudonymous` |
| `traceparent` | `traceparent` | supported | `pseudonymous` |
| `tracestate` | `tracestate` | supported | `pseudonymous` |

The adapter sanitizes `x-request-id` to printable ASCII at 128 characters and
generates a fresh id when it is absent or invalid. With the optional top-level
`tracing` provider configured, the adapter validates W3C `traceparent` and
`tracestate`, starts vendor-neutral spans for native HTTP and WebSocket work,
keeps context isolated across async operations, and exposes capture/injection on
`platform.trace`. The provider may return an OpenTelemetry Span directly.
Without a provider the tracing boundary is a no-op and allocates no spans.

## Data classes and retention defaults

| Class | Personal data | Default retention | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `operational` | no | `operator-policy` | Bounded framework state with no user identifier or payload |
| `pseudonymous` | yes | `minimum-needed` | Request or trace correlation identifiers |
| `application` | yes | `omit-unless-classified` | Application-supplied attributes that require deployer classification |
| `secret` | yes | `prohibited` | Credentials, cookies, authorization values, tokens, and payload secrets |

## Metric no-data laws

| Policy | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `registry_zero` | A registered counter exists at zero before its first event. |
| `zero_when_complete` | A complete snapshot emits the registered counter family at zero. |
| `last_sample` | A local gauge exists only after the registry has a value. |
| `incomplete_until_sampled` | A required unsampled gauge makes the snapshot incomplete. |
| `absent_when_unavailable` | An optional platform signal is absent when its source is unavailable. |
| `registry_histogram_zero` | A supported histogram registers zero buckets, count, and sum before its first observation. |
| `zero_when_registered` | A complete snapshot emits a zero histogram only when every worker registered that optional family. |
| `not_exposed` | A merge-owned signal is not exposed by a worker registry. |
| `always_present` | A successful snapshot always writes this completeness signal. |

A zero is never substituted for an unavailable optional source. Required
registered counters may produce a real zero only when every reporting worker
attests the family; a required unsampled gauge makes the snapshot incomplete.

registry may apply an operator prefix when serializing; cluster snapshots and
this manifest always use the canonical unprefixed names.
